answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit a job bid; the protocol randomly audits completed work, and a false claim forfeits that stake. One operator can still create many identities, but must fund each one separately, so splitting a reputation across umber, sparrow, and lotus accounts multiplies the capital at risk. The mechanism raises the cost of Sybil attacks rather than proving identities are unique, and honest agents recover their stake after passing audits.
